listing.name: Chocolate Doom
listing.summary: Play Doom with Chocolate Doom, or use the separate Chocolate Heretic, Hexen and Strife players with their matching game data.

steps.title: Choose your player on Windows
steps.instruction: The Windows download for this entry is the Chocolate Doom x86-64 ZIP. The publisher release offers separate chocolate-heretic, chocolate-hexen and chocolate-strife ZIPs. Keep the matching player, setup utility and DLLs together. Run the setup utility to configure controls and audio, then use the game executable to play.

steps.title: Select the IWAD for the game you want to play
steps.instruction: Point the matching player at your IWAD with -iwad followed by the file path. Chocolate Doom accepts Doom IWADs or the freely available Freedoom data. Use Heretic data with Chocolate Heretic, hexen.wad with Chocolate Hexen and strife1.wad with Chocolate Strife. Keep any accompanying Strife voice data with the IWAD. The engine packages contain no original game data.

warnings: Keep your actual IWADs, settings, saved games, autoload files and the creating runtime before changing versions or switching engine variants.
If a final text screen appears after you choose Quit, press a key to close the player.

references.title: Install a distribution package on Linux or Mac
references.instruction: Use your Linux distribution’s chocolate-doom package for all four players. Debian packages are available on x86-64 and ARM64. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac, use brew install chocolate-doom on a supported Homebrew host. Run the matching chocolate-doom, chocolate-heretic, chocolate-hexen or chocolate-strife command. Your package manager owns updates.

references.title: Find settings and saves
references.instruction: For a portable Windows copy, start the player in its own folder and keep the configuration and saves it writes there. On Linux the default profile is $XDG_DATA_HOME/chocolate-doom, normally ~/.local/share/chocolate-doom. On Mac it is normally ~/Library/Application Support/chocolate-doom. Preserve the actual paths if you use -config, -extraconfig or -savedir. The default per-game save folders can differ by IWAD.
